chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the slaughtered animal, and he said: 'If the tail moves, or the eyelid, or the ear, then it is validly slaughtered.'

key_terms.الذَّبِيحَة: The slaughtered animal; the object of ritual slaughter in Islamic law
key_terms.الطَّرْف: The eyelid or blinking of the eye; a sign of life used as a criterion for valid slaughter
key_terms.ذَكِيّ: Literally 'pure/intelligent'; in jurisprudential usage: an animal validly and lawfully slaughtered, whose meat is permissible (halal) to consume

ai.seo_question: What are the signs that indicate an animal was alive when slaughtered in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a legal ruling on the validity of an animal's slaughter. The Imam teaches that post-slaughter movement — specifically of the tail, eyelid, or ear — is sufficient evidence that the animal was alive at the time of slaughter, thus rendering it ritually pure (dhaki) and permissible to consume. This ruling was important for jurisprudence since the legal validity of slaughter depends on the animal being alive at the moment of the knife's cut.
